After managing spaceflight hardware development for NASA, Kellie McKeown transitioned to Television Broadcast where she successfully managed software and hardware development projects and organizations for Sony, Sportvision, Digidesign audio division of Avid, StorerTV and as director of engineering for TiVo. McKeown began McKeown Consulting in 1998. Her forte is guiding software vendors to evolve their engineering organizations, procedures, and processes to successfully deliver to large broadcast clients. McKeown graduated from Virginia Tech with a degree in Computer Science. Details at www.mckeownconsulting.tv and www.mckeownconsulting.com.

A SMPTE Fellow, Wendy Aylsworth has spent 26 years in entertainment technology, focusing on bringing emerging technologies into production and distribution usage. Her work has included introducing NextGen technologies to television, high-frame-rate capability to movie theaters, standardizing D-Cinema in SMPTE and ISO, and animation. Aylsworth is currently the Past President of SMPTE and volunteers at both the Television Academy and the Academy of Motion Pictures Arts & Sciences.

Renu Thomas is executive vice president, Media Operations, Engineering and IT for Disney|ABC Television Group. She reports to Ben Sherwood, co-chair, Disney Media Networks and president of Disney|ABC Television Group. Thomas ensures strategic alignment of investments, initiatives and business growth, including global expansion, new markets and new product/service development/deployment. Thomas was formerly senior vice president, Technology and Operations, Disney|ABC Networks Group responsible for direction and management of all television functions across U.S. Domestic Disney Channel, Disney XD, Disney Junior, Freeform (ABC Family), Disney|ABC Domestic Television (Syndication) and Radio Disney. Thomas joined The Walt Disney Company in 2007 as vice president of Operations for ABC News. Prior to joining, Thomas held a director of production position for MacNeil/Lehrer Productions and was director of Studio Operations at NBC Universal. Thomas graduated from Cornell University with a BS and ME in Operations Research & Industrial Engineering.

For more than 30 years, Andrea Berry has served as an award-winning broadcast media executive, for the Fox and CBS television networks. She led technical teams for high profile events including the World Series, the Olympic Winter Games, NFL, NCAA, and NASCAR. As a Broadcast Operations leader, Berry held key roles launching new cable and broadcast television networks and overseeing network Digital Media Management initiatives. Berry earned a bachelor's degree in computer science, minoring in electrical engineering from the Illinois Institute of Technology. She holds Executive Certificates in Management and Leadership from M.I.T. and in New Media Management from USC. An advocate for developing young people's skills in leadership and S.T.E.A.M. (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Math) education, Berry serves on the Boards of the NAB Education Foundation and the Sports Video Group. She was recently recognized by the Alliance for Women in Media for STEM Leadership in Media.

Marilyn Pierce began her television career after high school at the Dallas County Sheriff 's Department. After a stent at GTE doing installations and repairs, she returned to broadcasting at the Dallas PBS/NPR station as a master control operator. She's lived and breathed Master Control ever since. She worked up the engineering ladder from local stations to the national network operations center in Washington, D.C., as a senior engineer for PBS. She is now at Fox News Channel and Fox Business Network as one of the directors of engineering for master control and program distribution. Pierce has worked both sides of the broadcasting industry as vendor and customer.

Cindy Hutter Cavell joined Cavell Mertz & Associates technical consultants in 2010. As vice president and senior engineer, she assists TV and radio station clients in all phases of RF and technical facility engineering and design. She worked as director of engineering for Sprint Nextel during the 2 GHz BAS band relocation project, served as general manager for the Fox Sports Net nationwide program playout facilities, and has been chief engineer at several television stations across the country. Cavell spent 15 years as a field technical manager at ABC news prior to her foray into local television, managing large remote broadcasts overseas for news coverage. She participated in three Olympic Games for ABC, for which she shared in Emmy Awards for Technical Achievement. Cavell holds a B.S. degree in journalism from the University of Kansas.

Jennifer Zeidan started in the industry as an intern at Cisco System's Cisco TV in 2008 where she learned live television and master control. She transitioned to production engineer after graduating from Santa Clara University and began technical management of large-scale events and broadcasts for Cisco. Five years later, she found herself in a real-life “The Newsroom” at the Qatar-based news corporation Al Jazeera Media Network. As a broadcast engineer stationed in Al Jazeera America's San Francisco Bureau and AJ+ Headquarters, she helped launch Al Jazeera America and AJ+, Al Jazeera's newest digitalonly, millennial-geared network. After moving from corporate television to news, the time came to step into the world of film. Zeidan is now a media systems engineer at Lucasfilm's Industrial Light and Magic and enjoying new adventures in film.

John Hudson is director of strategic technology & international standardization for Semtech Gennum Products. His responsibilities include technology strategy, product definition and international standardization for Semtech's video and datacom business. Hudson has spent 28 years in the broadcast industry beginning his career as a design engineer at Sony Broadcast and Professional Europe. He joined Gennum in 1999 and has been instrumental in developing the company's video and multimedia semiconductor business. As an active member of SMPTE, SMPTE Fellow, and past Excellence in Standard Award Winner, Hudson serves as chair of the 32NF40 Working Group on SDI Interfaces and chairs the 32NF70 6G-SDI drafting group. He is the author of several SMPTE Standards, and actively contributes to the development of realtime Streaming Media Interfaces for Video and D-Cinema Production. Hudson attained a Higher National Diploma in electronics and communications engineering from the Farnborough College of Technology in 1988. He is the author of 11 patents on video processing and signal integrity solutions for multimedia applications and regularly contributes technical papers and presentations to seminars and technology events.

Nigel Seth-Smith joined Gennum in 2002 as part of a team responsible for strategic new product definition. He represents Gennum on the ITU-R and the DTG, where he chairs a working group on Flat Panel Displays used for Broadcast Monitoring. Prior to joining Gennum, Seth-Smith was in R&D design and engineering management at a number of organizations, including the UKIBA, Scientific-Atlanta, DPS and Snell & Wilcox. He has been a member of the IEE since 1982, and the IEEE since 1995. He has published a number of patents and papers, and has made presentations at IBC, Montreux, and ICCE.

Randy Conrod has been involved in the broadcast television industry for more than 30 years. Starting with broadcast video systems in 1982, he learned the ropes as a technician and progressed into technical sales. In 1990, he joined Leitch Technology as a sales engineer and moved into product marketing in 1998, focusing on audio and video processing and is currently senior product manager for digital products at Imagine Communications participating in product development for video, audio, data and metadata processing systems.

Marc Levy has more 20 years of industry experience in telecommunications and networking. He was introduced to telecommunications as part of a team developing the digital infrastructure for a microwave-based rural telephony system in his native South Africa. He later focused on Ethernet, and has 15 years experience in silicon implementations of high-speed (10G+) Ethernet. Levy was a founder of Octera, a technology startup that was acquired by Macnica in 2011. He now leads Macnica's IP product development in video transport over high-speed networks among other projects. Levy has extensive experience leading engineering teams architecting and developing complex products using leading-edge FPGA technology. He holds a degree in electrical engineering from the University of Cape Town, South Africa.

Laura (Reshetar) Richardson is a program manager and business development manager for design service and intellectual property at Macnica Americas, Inc. Before joining Macnica, Richardson served as an officer in the U.S. Navy as a diesel engine inspector. She has more than 13 years of military service to include tours in the Persian Gulf and Afghanistan. She holds a B.S. in political science and a minor in Russian from the United States Naval Academy.

Gaël Rouvroy is a leading expert in FPGA design specializing in image and video compression, secure and reconfigurable hardware encoders and decoders, cryptographic hardware, block ciphers, DRM, and watermarking. Rouvroy is co-founder and chief technology officer of intoPIX. He holds an electronics and mechanics engineering master's degree and Ph.D. from the Université catholique de Louvain (Belgium). He is active in several standardization committees (JPEG, VESA,…) and has presented more than 20 papers on compression, security, watermarking, and design strategies for cost-effective and low-power implementations.
